clue.text: A report I translated in South Africa

indicators.note: translated means these words are turned into a different form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone files a report that gets translated while working in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' asks for the letters of A REPORT I to be rearranged; the definition is a place 'in South Africa', its administrative capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital city of the Republic, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Perfect without the merest hint of any rain

parts.words: the merest hint of any rain
parts.note: a spot of rain is a single drop, the slightest sign of it
less can mean without, as in 'a sky less clouds'

explanation.surface: A perfect day has not even a drop of rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives 'without' first but the charade is in answer order: SPOT comes first, then LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a single mark or stain is flawless, hence perfect.

clue.text: The highest part of the church needs to be pointed

definitions.text: The highest part of the church needs to be pointed

parts.words: The highest part of the church needs to be pointed
parts.note: the tall tower of a church tapers to a point, and its brickwork, like any masonry, needs pointing with mortar

explanation.surface: A churchwarden notes that the top of the church needs mortar work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering spire tower is the loftiest part of a church building, and it rises to a point.

clue.text: Fool gets credit note and money

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
E is a musical note
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A fool is handed a credit note and some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN as money is dated British slang; E is one of the note names A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot or very stupid person, a common insult synonym for a fool.

clue.text: A word of cheer

parts.note: the reading is literal: an exclamation shouted to cheer, rather than a comforting remark

explanation.surface: Someone offers a few encouraging words.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation shouted in celebration or applause, literally a cheer.

clue.text: Fiddle just enough to pass

parts.note: a violinist scrapes the strings, and a candidate who does barely enough to pass an exam gets by narrowly

explanation.surface: A music student plays the violin just well enough to pass the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to succeed by the narrowest margin, and a fiddler scrapes the bow across the strings.

clue.text: Divide the cost of investment between us

definitions.text: Divide the cost of investment between us

parts.words: Divide the cost of investment between us
parts.note: partners splitting an outlay go halves on it, and a share is also a unit of investment

explanation.surface: Two partners agree to split the bill for a joint investment.
explanation.definitionFit: To split outgoings among several people is to go halves or fifty-fifty on spending.

clue.text: One will get distorted views here after reflection

definitions.text: One will get distorted views here after reflection

parts.words: One will get distorted views here after reflection
parts.note: the phrase sounds like someone muddled after thinking things over, but literally describes curved glass at a fairground

explanation.surface: Someone warns that brooding too long warps your opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground attraction lined with curved glass that bends your reflected image.

clue.text: Father has a way with the very thing despite being over the hill

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
ST, street, is a way or road
'it' is the very thing, as in 'that's it!'

explanation.surface: Dad has a road and the perfect gadget even though he is getting old.
explanation.definitionFit: Too old to be any good, an idiom for being elderly or declining.

clue.text: Charm with Hartnell fashion

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Norman Hartnell, the royal couturier, charms with his fashion designs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartnell was dressmaker to the Queen, so 'fashion' reads as couture, but it is the verb asking for an anagram of HARTNELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or hold spellbound someone is to charm them.

clue.text: Dog to go round the track once

definitions.text: Dog to go round the track once

parts.words: Dog to go round the track once
parts.note: a racing greyhound makes one circuit of the stadium course

explanation.surface: A greyhound is sent out for a single circuit of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A single circuit of a racetrack is a familiar sporting term.

clue.text: Transport of late

parts.note: 'of late' reads as 'recently', but 'the late' are the dead, and this vehicle carries them

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles about recent public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral vehicle that carries a coffin, conveying the deceased.

clue.text: Meal voucher

parts.note: the clue is a whole phrase for a meal ticket; the first word of its formal British name is wanted

explanation.surface: A worker is handed a ticket for food.
explanation.walkthrough: Luncheon vouchers were paper tickets British employers gave staff to buy a midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for a midday meal, as in the British employee meal ticket scheme.

clue.text: Is able to preserve fruit

definitions.meaning: has the ability, third person singular
to seal fruit in tins for keeping

explanation.surface: Someone is capable of bottling fruit for the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means is able in the third person, and as a verb also means to seal food in tins.

clue.text: Cooking vessels in the river over a wide area

indicators.note: in tells us the cooking vessels sit inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a favourite of setters
pans are vessels used for cooking

explanation.surface: Pots and pans have been dumped in a river across a broad area.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad stretch of land, sea or sky is a wide area.

clue.text: Born in France

parts.note: the French word meaning born, used in English before a married woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: Someone's birthplace was France.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French where it literally means born, used to give a woman's original surname.

clue.text: Right-winger brings back birds to eat

parts.note: CON is short for a Conservative, someone on the political right

indicators.note: brings back says the birds' word is read backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: A Tory returns from a shoot with birds for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour or take in food is to eat.

clue.text: Decisively defeated the Tories

parts.note: a beaten side or batsman is out
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: The Conservatives lost the election by a clear margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and conclusively, as in winning without question.

clue.text: Noticed it had moved sideways and was serrated

parts.note: saw means noticed
edged means moved gradually sideways

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a blade shift sideways and saw its jagged teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed like the blade of a cutting tool, jagged along the margin.

clue.text: Phrenologists leading the tribes?

parts.note: phrenologists read skull bumps so are jokingly men of the head; tribal chiefs are the other sense

explanation.surface: Skull-readers have taken charge of the clans.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefs of villages or tribes, and punningly experts on skulls.

clue.text: Trees and sea formed by pieces of mosaic

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trees and sea are depicted in a mosaic picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges the letters of TREES and SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Small square tiles of stone or glass used to make a decorative floor or wall picture.

clue.text: Some artiste rolling in alcohol

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer is rolling about drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'in alcohol' is wrong: 'in' is a link word, and only 'alcohol' defines, since the answer is a type of alcohol, not something inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically it is a steroid alcohol, such as cholesterol, so a kind of alcohol.

clue.text: Sets right with a parting word in Spanish

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone sorts things out with a Spanish farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless receivers are sets, as in a television or wireless set.

clue.text: Attempt to hide another wad that is cheap and showy

indicators.note: to hide means the try is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: try means attempt

indicators.note: another treats the letters of wad as another arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A forger tries to conceal a second bundle of notes, a vulgar trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges WAD into AWD, and 'to hide' puts that inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy and of poor quality, flashy but tacky.

clue.text: Ray resorted to a place in Scotland?

indicators.note: re-sorted means sorted again, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Ray went off on holiday to a Scottish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' looks like 'went to a resort' but splits as re-sorted, an anagram signal; the town is itself a resort on the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the west coast of the country, in Ayrshire.

clue.text: Went up as many finished

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many
ended means finished

explanation.surface: Lots of people climbed as the event came to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbed or rose, the past tense of going upwards.

clue.text: Fashionable entrance being within a building

parts.note: in means fashionable
a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A stylish doorway is found inside a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated or happening inside, under a roof rather than outdoors.

clue.text: Take one's socks off and run away

definitions.meaning: with bare feet the backs of the feet are exposed
flee, the idiom for running off so fast pursuers see only your back

explanation.surface: Someone removes their socks and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing socks exposes the backs of the feet, and the idiom means to flee quickly.
